scope: Standalone GNU grep compatibility adapter, private Bash scope and optional Pi native Bash integration

requirements.contract: Qualified text and GNU -l/-L searches use rg while retaining GNU file coverage, byte identity and observable results, including hidden/ignored files and qualified binary filename matches.
GNU short/long options, combinations, abbreviations, argument ordering, pattern sources and help/version remain accepted; invalid invocations retain GNU diagnostics.

Qualified fixed, basic and extended matchers preserve GNU record selection. Qualified Perl matchers may use rg in C/POSIX byte locales; UTF-8-locale -P and other unqualified regex/locale semantics use the original GNU invocation.

Operand order, r/R symlink behavior, cycle warnings, ordered include/exclude/exclude-from rules, directory/device modes, stdin labels and filename-prefix defaults preserve GNU selection. Invalid UTF-8 filenames request native execution before output.
Counts, filenames with/without matches, only-matching spans, line/byte prefixes, context groups and NUL separators retain GNU output semantics for translated inputs.

Every valid GNU call executes without adapter guidance, blocking or a caller retry; unqualified binary, regex, locale, colour, special-file, pattern-file and traversal semantics automatically use unchanged GNU argv before consuming stdin or publishing output. Compatibility acceptance does not imply universal rg acceleration.

Pattern-file expansion and traversal metadata remain bounded; expansions too large for the rg argument budget retain the original GNU invocation instead of failing with argv overflow or truncating search coverage.
Stdin pattern files and early-exit stdin m/l/L/q searches retain GNU stream ownership and unread-byte position; qualified ordinary stdin filters may use rg.

The shell-prefix helper installs a private non-exported grep function in the chosen Bash command. The optional Pi extension gates its native bash tool by exact provider name (default qwen-r9700). Other providers, Pi user ! commands, ordinary shells, explicit command/absolute-path bypasses and child scripts remain native. Quoting, globs and pipelines retain their usual semantics; valid Unicode argv may qualify after raw UTF-8 validation, while invalid byte argv remain original GNU without JavaScript decoding.

No-match and filesystem failures preserve exit statuses 1 and 2, missing files remain visible, quiet-mode selection retains GNU status precedence, and failed inputs produce no fabricated matches/counts.

Seeded distinct matcher/flag/locale/byte cases compare qualified rg output/status to GNU, require documented native fallback for irreducible semantics, preserve case seeds and separate actual rg comparisons from fallback oracle classifications.

Generated distinct full-CLI combinations compare actual wrapper stdout/stderr/status with GNU and independently verify that selected qualified cases execute rg rather than receiving fallback-only credit.

Varied synthetic trees and operand/filter sequences preserve exact GNU CLI output/status; narrowing cannot introduce paths, repeated operands preserve multiplicity and dereference recursion retains ordinary recursive matches.
Actual pseudoterminal execution preserves GNU auto-color behavior for ordinary and dumb terminals without changing streamed byte output.

Malformed, fragmented and truncated rg records, reader/spawn/dependency errors, slow consumers and broken output streams produce appropriate completion/error status without fabricated counts or orphaned owned children.
Test-only count, byte-prefix and no-match-status mutations must be rejected by semantic output/status oracles; syntax and infrastructure failures do not receive mutation credit.

requirements.owner: GNU option parser and compatibility boundary
requirements.contract: An independently enumerated GNU option inventory is checked against installed GNU help; all ordered representative spelling pairs, repeated/conflicting options, the complete selected boolean-flag power set and numeric/enum/form boundaries compare actual wrapper stdout/stderr/status to GNU. Coverage counts and finite scope are explicit; arbitrary argv strings are unbounded.

The installed executable forwards GNU argv without reserving wrapper options, preserves exact stdout/stderr/status and stdin, and the emitted prefix adapts only private Bash grep calls with safe paths containing shell metacharacters.

An actual npm pack tarball extracts without source-tree dependency, contains the verification runner and synthetic regression suites, and its executable and shell-prefix helper retain GNU output/status and scope semantics.

Ordinary regular-file searches without -a and without-match binary mode may use rg only after every selected file passes complete text classification through fixed 64 KiB chunks. Payload size and selected occurrences have no former 16 MiB/4096 cutoff. NUL, malformed UTF-8 in UTF-8 locales and proof-required stdin preserve original GNU invocation before search output. Late bytes after 17 MiB and actual rg invocations are independently verified; classification still reads each selected file completely.

C.UTF-8 ASCII patterns and complete ASCII subjects avoid scalar scans and use compatible C matching through actual rg. Valid Unicode subjects use separately verified GNU scalar tables; proof-required stdin stays original GNU. PCRE-only POSIX class names preserve GNU invalid-class diagnostics.

requirements.owner: GNU literal extraction and color formatter
requirements.contract: Case-sensitive fixed or wholly literal BRE/ERE patterns without word or whole-line restrictions use real rg for selected records and reproduce GNU leftmost-longest literal byte spans for extraction/highlighting, including repeated/newline/empty needles, raw subject bytes, NUL records, and max-count trailing context. Inverted universal patterns remain an explicitly tested native boundary.

BRE/ERE selection over regular NUL-separated files preserves GNU record anchors, newline-inclusive dot, whole-record and word matching through actual rg. POSIX extraction uses candidate-only spans when needed. Inverse max-count trailing context is independently compared through actual rg. Complete UTF-8 proof permits NUL delimiters and rejects malformed bytes; Perl NUL matching remains separately gated.

requirements.owner: GNU span broker after rg record selection
requirements.contract: General BRE/ERE extraction and coloring obtain leftmost-longest spans only from private records actually selected by rg, preserving prefixes, NUL records, context and max-count boundaries. GNU syntax validation precedes rg and invalid syntax retains original diagnostics. Candidate-content assertions reject passing original unselected records to the span helper.

SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP cancel the owned candidate span child, reap ignored-signal helpers, remove private spools and return conventional status. Cancellation during collection publishes no partial records. Cancellation after replay begins exits public/private CLI entries even with unread stdout, without bogus truncated-JSON diagnostics.

requirements.owner: GNU locale tables with actual rg searches
requirements.contract: Fully validated UTF-8 regular subjects use native GNU scalar membership and case closure to translate fixed matching and ordinary BRE/ERE brackets, classes, ranges and word escapes. Tests compare Latin/Greek/Turkish/Kelvin/sigma/sharp-S cases, numbered captures and multiple patterns, NUL membership and outputs against full independent GNU invocations and require real rg searches. Invalid GNU ranges, insensitive backreferences, malformed UTF-8 and proof-required stdin remain explicit native controls. Ordinary Unicode brackets under nontrivial collation remain original GNU; an owned Czech locale independently proves multichar ch behavior.

An owned private cache avoids repeated scalar scans; corrupted tables and changed GNU executable identity force fresh proof. In one process, replacing an owned LOCPATH English locale with Turkish under the same name/path changes real rg matching according to the new GNU oracle. Custom locale tables cannot reuse stale global memory. Tests never mutate system locales, the default cache or installed programs.

Public and private calls preserve auxiliary FD3, FD63 and FD4097 for operands/patterns/process substitutions without exposing closed descriptors. Span-helper files coexist with caller descriptors. Closed standard input/output/error retain exact GNU output, errors and status through direct executables without recording wrappers.

Each GNU -e pattern retains its own numbered backreferences when rg combines alternatives, including different one/two/three capture counts, extraction, color/context, C and C.UTF-8, and the private Bash route. A disposable source mutant disabling branch-reset grouping is rejected by a full GNU output oracle without syntax failures.

requirements.owner: rg record selection and GNU candidate span adapter
requirements.contract: Qualified -F -w -x -o uses actual rg selection and candidate-only GNU spans, preserving release-specific record terminators and color boundaries. Independent full GNU comparisons cover LF/NUL, empty/punctuation/repeated/newline/file pattern sources, prefixes, empty colors, C/C.UTF-8 folding, Unicode private Bash calls, inverse/max-count/context and repeated operands. Existing full finite option subsets retain exact GNU mismatch assertions.

Linux -U/--binary is an accepted no-op and qualified cases execute real rg. Exact GNU oracles cover selection, prefixes, extraction/color, context, counts, names, quiet, NUL and raw subject bytes. Binary detection, malformed default UTF-8, invalid syntax and early-exit stdin retain original GNU with no engine credit; non-Linux platforms remain native.

After real rg selection and private GNU spans, replay honors stdout drain between formatter records. A paused owned sink keeps the normal writable queue within128KiB while output remains byte-exact to GNU; a disposable no-drain source mutant exceeds the bound. Product and negative-control comparisons/invocations are counted separately.

requirements.owner: native aggregate/text dispatcher and shared Bash/CLI lane
requirements.contract: Automatic routes use native parse/metadata and parallel rg without Node; compatible large aggregate and sparse explicit-text workloads retain exact GNU output bytes, order, diagnostics and status. Bounded record reads/output publication, scale/dense short-circuit/unsafe syntax/stream/locale/error boundaries select original GNU. Finite option audit and real CLI/function timings include startup, metadata and output ordering. Optional experimental adapter remains independently verified.
